title: Cross-environment Cooperation Enables Zero-shot Multi-agent Coordination
summary: A fully admissible Forced Coordination layout satisfies the stated local accessibility rule but is unsolvable because onions cannot cross the partition to any pot. The printed meta-game also admits a locally stable IPPO/FCP mixture; historical held-out protocol impact remains unresolved.
limitations: No empirical reproduction or raw human-data inferential reanalysis.

problems.title: Locally accessible generated layout can be unsolvable

source_claim.location: Abstract pp.1-2; A.1 p.14; Algorithm 1 p.15
source_claim.paraphrase: At least one reachable facility of each type and agents on opposite sides guarantee a solvable task.

assumptions: two empty-inventory agents at 6 and 8 (zero-based row-major)
held-out set can consist of five canonical tasks, none equal to this layout
problems.check: Static source confirms all admissible placements. Independent graph calculation verifies left component {6,11,16}, right {8,13,18}, shared boundary {7,12,17}, each containing plate pile, plate pile, goal. Right-side onions remain absent under all legal actions; all pots are on the right. Induction proves no delivery is reachable.
counterevidence: Shared onion dispensers or pots can make other split layouts solvable, but are absent here.
Random prefilled inventories are excluded by the standard empty initialization.
No claim that the particular layout appeared in historical samples.
problems.core_dependency: Core contribution 2 and comparison with prior generators expressly require solvable task infrastructure.
problems.impact: Invalidates universal solvability guarantee; does not estimate prevalence or overturn measured CEC benefits.

correction.supported_bound: A repair must certify material-flow/delivery feasibility in addition to local accessibility; no full corrected generator is asserted.

problems.title: Original-task meta-game has a stable non-CEC attractor

source_claim.location: Section 6 Q1 p.7, Fig.8; A.8 p.19, Fig.21 p.20
source_claim.paraphrase: Dynamics point toward CEC or CEC-Finetune for both task settings.

problems.check: x=(11/24,0,13/24,0,0) has equal resident payoff 781/1200. E3T/CEC/CEC-FT invasion rates are -71/240,-97/800,-1/24. Edge eigenvalue -143/1200. Negative invasion margins persist under symmetric rounding errors <=.005.
problems.result: Locally asymptotically stable mixture without CEC; additional basin beyond CEC-FT.
counterevidence: Pure CEC-FT is itself locally stable.
Fig.8 top-left already shows directions toward lower edge.
Procedural-task matrix and human study are separate evidence.
problems.core_dependency: A bounded interpretation of one supporting meta-game; the principal empirical comparisons do not require global attraction.
problems.impact: Qualify dynamical interpretation; no demonstrated reversal of primary empirical result.

correction.statement: The original-task meta-game admits both CEC-FT attraction and a stable IPPO/FCP mixture.

problems.title: One-shot held-out rejection in release leaves historical separation unresolved

source_claim.location: A.1 pp.14-15 and Algorithm 1; overcooked.py lines 243-257
source_claim.paraphrase: Repeat generation until outside held-out set.

assumptions: Inspection of fixed source commit only
q^2 illustration additionally assumes independent draws with held-out probability q
problems.check: Released reset conditionally replaces once without rechecking; config default check_held_out=False is not evidence of historical CEC configuration. Initialization does construct held-out collection.
problems.result: Implementation does not certify strict rejection; historical overlap not established.
counterevidence: Default configuration is single-task and may have been overridden.
Incidence and significance could be negligible or absent.
problems.core_dependency: Strict unseen-task interpretation depends on actual historical configuration and sampled tasks.
problems.impact: Needs original run records; does not establish published contamination.

correction.statement: Repeated rejection gives strict exclusion when probability of an admissible draw is positive; implementation not verified.
